question: Which of the following disease does NOT spread through the air?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cholera**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cholera does not spread through the air, and is instead a waterborne disease: 
 
• Cholera
 
• A waterborne disease that is primarily transmitted through contaminated food and water. 
 
• Airborne diseases
 
 
• Diseases that are caused by pathogens and transmitted through the air, such as the common cold, pneumonia, and tuberculosis.
 
• Pathogens can be viruses, bacteria, or fungi, and are spread through coughing, sneezing, dust, and spraying of liquids. 
 
 
 
• HIV-AIDS is another disease that does not spread through the air but is instead sexually transmitted.
 
• It can be transmitted through direct sexual contact, using infected blood or syringe, and from the infected mother to its child during pregnancy or via breastfeeding

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus, causing cough with phlegm or pus, fever, chills, and difficulty breathing
 
 
• Pneumonia can be caused by various pathogens,
 
 
• including bacteria (e.g., Streptococcus pneumoniae), viruses (e.g., influenza virus), and fungi. It can also develop after inhaling irritants or as a complication of another illness.
 
 
 
 
 
• Tuberculosis is a contagious bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily affecting the lungs but can also impact other parts of the body.
 
 
• TB is spread through airborne particles when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
 
• Close and prolonged contact with an infected person increases the risk of transmission.
 
 
 
• The common cold is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract, primarily caused by rhinoviruses.
 
 
• Cold viruses are highly contagious and can be spread through respiratory droplets, direct contact with infected surfaces, or close contact with an infected person.
